previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted due to recurrent hypoglycemia with a blood glucose of 43, accompanied by increased drainage and pain at her G-tube site. Imaging confirmed the G-tube was correctly positioned with no leakage, and contrast passed normally into the colon. She was restarted on metronidazole for small intestinal bacterial overgrowth, which may contribute to hypoglycemia. Granulation tissue at the G-tube site was treated with silver nitrate and mupirocin ointment. A fasting hypoglycemia work-up was completed, with labs drawn during a monitored fast before resuming feeds. She remained stable with blood glucose levels between 55 and 110, and was discharged home with new medications including octreotide and acarbose, instructions for wound care, and follow-up with her endocrinologist.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ was a direct admit to the Bariatric Service with 
multiple episodes of hypoglycemia a/w confusion and short term 
memory loss. Upon her admission, the Neurology, Endocrine, and 
Gastrointestinal teams were consulted. Tube feeds were cycled at 
20 during the day and 40 at night and multiple lab tests were 
ordered. The Neurology team determined no additional imaging 
studies were necessary and that her symptoms were likely related 
to the hypoglycemia. The ___ team performed a fasting study 
by d/c daytime tube feed at 1300 on ___ and requested a 
glucose, C pep, cortisol, and pro insulin if <55mg/dL. Her 
fingersticks did not drop below the threshold during her stay 
and therefore the labs were not obtained. The team however, 
replaced her meter and strips because the meter was showing 
values that were not significantly lower than her fingerstick 
values. The GI team performed an EGD on ___ and no acute 
process was identified. In addition they stopped her Flagyl for 
bacterial overgrowth and changed Zofran to Compazine. During her 
hospital stay, her fingerstick did not drop below 78.  She was 
discharged with a plan for tube feeds from 11pm-7am at a rate of 
40 supplemented with a complex carbohydrate diet explained to 
her by the nutrition team. She will follow up with Dr. ___ 
in ___ weeks.
